title: Azure Firewall Threat Intelligence Hits

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:diagnostics` events with `Category="AzureFirewallApplicationRule" msg_s="*ThreatIntel*"` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.2.36 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:diagnostics` traffic without `Category="AzureFirewallApplicationRule" msg_s="*ThreatIntel*"`. Confirm UC-4.2.36 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:diagnostics` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" Category="AzureFirewallApplicationRule" msg_s="*ThreatIntel*"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.36_azure_firewall_threat_in_36"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.2.36 — Azure Firewall Threat Intelligence Hits: queries Microsoft Azure `mscs:azure:diagnostics` for search criteria `Category="AzureFirewallApplicationRule" msg_s="*ThreatIntel*"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Azure Firewall Threat Intelligence Hits' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.2.36 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable Threat Intel mode on Firewall and full diagnostic logging. Parse rule collection and threat category. Alert on new destination countries or sudden hit rate increase. Tune false positives with application owners.
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:diagnostics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable Threat Intel mode on Firewall and full diagnostic logging. Parse rule collection and threat category. Alert on new destination countries or sudden hit rate increase. Tune false positives with application owners.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" Category="AzureFirewallApplicationRule" msg_s="*ThreatIntel*"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.36_azure_firewall_threat_in_36"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:diagnostics` in `index=azure` to detect azure firewall threat intelligence hits. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_36_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Map (source IP), Table (FQDN, count), Timeline (hits)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure firewall threat intelligence hits so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
